title: Candidate anti-pattern: copying local gateway conveniences into production defaults
summary: Do not copy a detailed public health payload, Docker-socket or privileged local container access, plaintext fail-open encryption, optimistic readiness, or mutable latest-version deployment into production without an explicit threat and operations review.
incompatible_when: A development-only environment has no sensitive data, no untrusted clients, and the convenience is explicitly prevented from reaching production.
procedure: Expose only the minimum unauthenticated liveness signal; protect detailed diagnostics.
Remove Docker-socket, host, or privileged container access unless a reviewed production requirement proves it necessary.
Fail closed when required encryption is absent or fails; separate legacy migration behavior from production write behavior.
Base readiness on required dependency and initialization state, not only process startup.
Deploy immutable versions or digests and verify the installed identity instead of installing a mutable latest tag.
verification: Threat-model health, container, storage, and deployment boundaries for the target environment.
Test missing encryption configuration, encryption failure, dependency failure during startup, unauthenticated health access, and rollback to an immutable artifact.
rollback: Restore the previous production configuration or immutable artifact and disable the convenience path until its boundary has been reviewed.

confidence.rationale: The source directly shows these convenience behaviors; suitability depends on environment, so this remains a warning candidate rather than a claim of vulnerability.
